cover.title:
Three-way
**partition**
cover.lead: Only three kinds of values to group in place: three pointers, one pass.
cover.use_it_when: The array holds three kinds of values (like 0, 1, 2) to group in place.
cover.why_it_matters: Quick sort (post 26) uses the same idea to split around a pivot.

slides.title: Three piles
slides.scene: Sorting laundry on one rail: whites go to the front, darks to the back, colours stay where they are.

blocks.text: Each piece is looked at once and moved [[at most once]].

slides.title: Four zones
slides.lead: low and high fence off finished 0s and 2s. Everything from mid to high is still unchecked.

blocks.text: 0s before low, 1s from low to mid, unchecked up to high, 2s after.

quickcheck.question: Three-way partition on 2 0 1. How many loop steps does it take?
quickcheck.answer: Answer: {{loop_steps([2, 0, 1])}}. The 2 swaps back, the 1 comes in, then the 0 goes to the front.

slides.label: WHY MID STAYS
slides.teaser: The answer, then why mid stays
slides.title: Check what came back

blocks.label: AFTER A SWAP WITH HIGH
blocks.text: The number that came back from high is [[unchecked]]. mid stays to look at it.
After a swap with low, the number that came back was already checked, so mid moves on.

slides.title: Sort colors
slides.explain: 0 swaps to low, 1 stays, 2 swaps to high; then mid stays.

slides.teaser: The bug that leaves a 0 behind
slides.title: mid stays after high
slides.lead: Move mid after swapping with high and the number that came back is skipped.

wrong.note: The 0 from the back is never checked.

cost.note: One pass and in place. Counting works too, but takes two passes.

problems.title: Sort Array By Parity
problems.note: Two zones this time: evens, then odds.

problems.title: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
problems.note: Same three groups, but keep their order.

blog.summary: Only three kinds of values to group in place: three pointers, one pass.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (one value, all equal, reversed, the trap input 1 2 0) and random arrays of up to 14 values from 0 to 2, plus one array of 300 values
blog.tested_extra: The steps, the loop count and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: Three-way partition for LeetCode 75 Sort Colors: low, mid and high pointers group 0s, 1s and 2s in one pass.
lines: A 0 swaps to low, a 1 stays, a 2 swaps to high.
The trap: move mid after the high swap and 1 2 0 becomes 1 0 2.
